structured_output.world_model: W6: time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost is a pixel-proportional compute part plus a bandwidth-bound part. The simplest model of the surprises is that late freezes are cheap in accuracy and large in time, because they also skip BN/GELU backward, the optimizer update and Lookahead traffic. Early or stem-architecture changes cost accuracy at a worse rate than the epoch dial (E037, E051). The tip's population mean is ~0.752, only ~0.2 pp over the bar. 3-seed noise is ±0.3 pp from build-to-build kernel reselection, so accuracy ranges must be wide. Time noise is ~±0.04 s. Extending the group-2 freeze from 10% to 15% of steps should save ~0.1 s. Intermittent stem backward in the 28 px phase should save ~0.15 s, because the 28 px phase has the most steps. A group-1 freeze at 71% should save ~0.05 s and cost some accuracy. ReLU should save under 3%.

forecasts.reason: The extra 12 frozen steps save ~0.08 s. The accuracy cost is likely ~0.1 pp, which is within the noise on 3 seeds.
Skipping stem backward on half the 28 px steps saves about 0.12 s. The accuracy effect is a small loss that the 3-seed noise hides.
Only 4% more steps are frozen, so the time saving is small. The accuracy cost is probably a few hundredths of a pp up to ~0.2 pp.
The offline profile will likely project a 1–3% saving. That is below the 3% gate, so step 2 probably does not run. If it does run, accuracy would be slightly lower.
The stacking is conditional on earlier results. The top-up cost roughly cancels the cut savings, so time ends near the tip.

cruxes: Is the accuracy cost of the group-2 freeze linear in dose, or does it have a cliff like E037's? That decides whether I083 and I087 pay.
What is the true unselected population mean of the tip (~0.752 vs ~0.7535)? It decides whether any further time cut is feasible at all.
Does stem backward need steady updates, or only the 28→32 adaptation? This decides I084 and I085.
